title: Valid Palindrome
description: Decide whether a text line reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case and punctuation.
inputFormat:
The input is read from standard input as exactly one line:

1. Line 1: the text to test. It may contain ASCII letters, digits, spaces and punctuation characters, and it never contains a newline. Read the whole line - do not split it on spaces.
outputFormat: Print a single line containing the lowercase word `true` if the cleaned text is a palindrome, otherwise the lowercase word `false`.
constraints: The line contains printable ASCII characters only (no newline inside it)
Only ASCII letters and ASCII digits count as alphanumeric; other characters are ignored
notes: The comparison is case-insensitive, so `0P` is `false` while `0p` is `true`. Because the input line is guaranteed non-empty you never have to deal with a truly empty line, but a line made only of punctuation cleans down to the empty string and is still a palindrome.

testCases.input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
testCases.explanation:
Step 1: drop every character that is not a letter or a digit, giving `amanaplanacanalpanama`.
Step 2: lower-case it, because the comparison ignores case.
Step 3: read the cleaned string forwards (`amanaplanacanalpanama`) and backwards (`amanaplanacanalpanama`) - they are identical, so print `true`.

Step 1: remove the space and lower-case the rest: `raceacar`.
Step 2: the first half `race` reversed is `ecar`, which does not match the second half `acar`.
Step 3: the string differs from its reverse, so print `false`.

Step 1: both characters survive filtering, so the cleaned string is `0p`.
Step 2: its reverse is `p0`, which is different.
Step 3: the two sides differ, so print `false`.
